recognizable_same_product.evidence: The rendered object in Image 2 shows a laptop with an open lid and visible keyboard/trackpad area, which is inconsistent with the closed, right-side profile view of the MacBook Air shown in Image 1. The render also displays an abstract screen pattern and lacks the clean aluminum finish and precise port placement (single 3.5mm jack) that define the official product identity.

major_proportions_plausible.evidence: The proportions of the rendered laptop are implausible: the lid appears disproportionately thick relative to the base, the hinge area is malformed, and the overall silhouette does not match the thin, uniform two-slab geometry of the MacBook Air M3 13-inch as seen in Image 1.

missing_or_invented_major_parts.evidence: Major parts are missing or invented: the single 3.5mm jack on the right side is absent; instead, the render shows undefined ports and structural deformities along the base edge. The screen displays an invented abstract pattern rather than a realistic display bezel. The keyboard and trackpad are exposed in a way inconsistent with the closed-profile reference image.

verdict_reason: The rendered object fails to establish recognizable identity as the same product/model family due to incorrect orientation, implausible proportions, and missing/invented major components. This is the second and final attempt; strict Stage B gate criteria are not met.
